Definition: an offence, or a sacrifice for it
BiblicalUsage: This word is both the offence and the offering for it, sin and sin offering in one. Abimelech calls what Abraham brought on his kingdom a great sin, Moses confronts Aaron over the great sin of the calf, and Jeroboam is charged with making Israel sin a great sin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the double meaning is the gospel in miniature: the sin and the offering for the sin share one word, because God meets the offence with the sacrifice. Sin is never named without the remedy standing beside it, and that is why I trust Him with my own.
RelatedEvents: Abraham and Abimelech; The Golden Calf; Fall of Samaria
